provenance: DBCAS-authored curriculum metadata grounded in the PostgreSQL 17 documentation (postgresql.org/docs/17) and standard database-engineering references (Elmasri & Navathe; Silberschatz, Korth & Sudarshan; Garcia-Molina, Ullman & Widom). Technically authored; not an instructor approval.
language_note: The concept table has no localized columns; concept metadata is English-only by schema. Vietnamese remains supported for question content, options, rubrics and UI strings.

SELECT.description: Retrieve rows and columns from a single table with SELECT, choosing projected values, filtering rows with WHERE and controlling presentation order.
learning_objectives: Identify the clauses that form a basic SELECT statement and the logical order in which they are evaluated.
Choose the columns and expressions needed to produce a requested result set.
Filter source rows with a WHERE predicate and explain how NULL affects the comparison.
Order result rows explicitly whenever the presentation order matters.

JOIN.description: Combine rows from two or more related relations with join predicates, distinguishing inner from outer joins and controlling row multiplication.
learning_objectives: Write an inner join that combines rows from two tables on a matching key.
Compare inner, left, right and full outer joins when unmatched rows must be preserved.
Explain how a missing or non-unique join key changes the number of returned rows.
Choose explicit JOIN ... ON syntax over implicit comma joins in new queries.

IDX.description: Use database indexes to accelerate selective lookups and joins while accounting for their write, storage and maintenance costs.
learning_objectives: Explain how an index avoids a sequential scan for a selective predicate.
Decide which columns and column order belong in a composite index for a query workload.
Compare the read benefit of an index with its write and storage overhead.
Verify index use through EXPLAIN instead of assuming the planner will choose it.

SQL-SELECT.description: Project columns and computed expressions from a table with SELECT, control duplicate rows and assign readable output column names.
learning_objectives: Project the required columns and expressions in a SELECT list.
Assign readable output names with column aliases.
Remove duplicate result rows with DISTINCT and state the cost of doing so.
Predict the result columns produced by SELECT * and by an explicit column list.

SQL-WHERE.description: Filter source rows with a boolean WHERE predicate that combines comparison, range, membership and NULL-aware conditions.
learning_objectives: Build a WHERE predicate that keeps exactly the rows required by a specification.
Combine conditions with AND, OR and NOT while respecting operator precedence.
Use IS NULL and IS NOT NULL instead of equality when NULL values are involved.
Explain why a predicate that compares with NULL yields unknown rather than true.

SQL-JOIN.description: Combine rows from related tables with JOIN, writing correct ON predicates and selecting the join type that matches the required result.
learning_objectives: Translate a relationship between tables into a correct JOIN ... ON condition.
Choose an inner or outer join based on whether unmatched rows must be kept.
Diagnose unexpected duplicate rows caused by a one-to-many join key.
Join three or more tables without losing the intended row population.

SQL-GROUP.description: Group rows into sets with GROUP BY and compute per-group aggregates such as counts, sums and averages.
learning_objectives: Group rows by one or more columns to produce one output row per group.
Apply aggregate functions to summarize each group.
Distinguish a grouping column from an aggregated expression in the SELECT list.
Explain how a NULL grouping key forms its own group.

SQL-HAVING.description: Filter grouped results with HAVING, distinguishing group-level predicates from row-level WHERE conditions.
learning_objectives: Apply HAVING to keep only groups that satisfy an aggregate condition.
Choose WHERE for row filtering and HAVING for group filtering inside the same query.
Explain why a WHERE clause cannot reference an aggregate result directly.
Predict the difference in output when a predicate moves from WHERE to HAVING.

SQL-SUBQUERY.description: Compose queries with scalar, row, IN, EXISTS and correlated subqueries in the SELECT, FROM and WHERE clauses.
learning_objectives: Use a scalar subquery where a single computed value is required.
Compare IN, EXISTS and join formulations for the same filtering task.
Write a correlated subquery that references the current outer row.
Explain when a subquery in FROM acts as an independent derived table.

DB-ER.description: Model a problem domain as entities, attributes and relationships, then translate the model into a relational schema with keys.
learning_objectives: Identify entities, attributes and relationships from a written domain description.
Determine cardinality and participation constraints for each relationship.
Convert an ER model into tables with primary and foreign keys.
Detect modeling choices that would duplicate data or lose required relationships.

DB-NORM.description: Evaluate relational schemas with functional dependencies and normal forms, and decompose them to reduce redundancy and update anomalies.
learning_objectives: Explain which update, insert and delete anomalies normalization is intended to prevent.
Derive candidate keys from a set of functional dependencies.
Decompose a relation into higher normal forms while preserving its dependencies.
Verify that a decomposition is lossless and does not fabricate rows.

DB-FD.description: Reason about functional dependencies, attribute closure and candidate keys as the theoretical basis for relational design.
learning_objectives: Determine whether a functional dependency is implied by a given set of dependencies.
Compute the attribute closure of a determinant.
Derive all candidate keys of a relation from its functional dependencies.
Use inference rules to simplify a dependency set without changing its closure.

DB-1NF.description: Apply first normal form by keeping every attribute atomic and eliminating repeating groups from relational tables.
learning_objectives: Identify repeating groups and multivalued cells that violate first normal form.
Restructure a non-atomic table into rows whose attribute values are atomic.
Explain why storing lists in a single column complicates querying and constraints.
Distinguish the requirements of first normal form from those of higher normal forms.

DB-2NF.description: Apply second normal form by removing partial dependencies of non-key attributes on part of a composite candidate key.
learning_objectives: Detect a partial dependency on part of a composite candidate key.
Decompose a relation in first normal form into second normal form.
Explain why second normal form is automatic when the key is a single attribute.
Verify that the resulting decomposition preserves the original information.

DB-3NF.description: Apply third normal form by eliminating transitive dependencies of non-key attributes on other non-key attributes.
learning_objectives: Detect transitive dependencies among non-key attributes.
Decompose a second-normal-form relation into third normal form.
Compare third normal form with Boyce-Codd normal form for a given schema.
Explain the redundancy that a transitive dependency introduces.

SQL-DML-KNOW.description: Explain the semantics of INSERT, UPDATE and DELETE, including predicates, constraints and transaction effects, without executing mutations in the learner sandbox.
learning_objectives: Describe how INSERT, UPDATE and DELETE change table contents.
Predict which rows an UPDATE or DELETE affects from its WHERE predicate.
Explain how constraints can reject or cascade a data modification.
State why destructive DML is assessed conceptually rather than executed in the read-only sandbox.

SQL-DDL-KNOW.description: Explain schema-definition statements, keys and constraints, and the effects of altering an existing table without executing DDL in the learner sandbox.
learning_objectives: Describe how CREATE TABLE declares columns, data types and constraints.
Distinguish primary keys, unique constraints, foreign keys and CHECK constraints.
Predict the impact of an ALTER TABLE operation on existing rows.
Explain why schema changes are assessed conceptually in the read-only sandbox.

E2E-TC1.description: Administrator end-to-end verification concept; it exists only to exercise curriculum CRUD and prerequisite editing and is safe to ignore in academic reporting.
learning_objectives: Exercise administrator concept editing in automated end-to-end verification.
Exercise prerequisite edge editing for a disposable curriculum record.
Confirm test-only curriculum records stay outside published assessment scope.

E2E-TC2.description: Secondary administrator end-to-end verification concept retained for prerequisite and deletion-guard checks in automated tests.
learning_objectives: Provide a second disposable concept for prerequisite and reference-guard tests.
Confirm reference guards prevent deletion while automated fixtures still reference the record.
Keep test-only curriculum data separate from published assessments.

PG-SYNTAX.description: Identifiers, keywords, constants, dollar quoting and operator structure of PostgreSQL statements.
learning_objectives: Identify the lexical elements that make up a PostgreSQL SQL statement.
Distinguish quoted identifiers from string constants in PostgreSQL syntax.
Use dollar quoting to embed multi-line or quote-heavy text safely.
Explain how operator tokens and comments are recognized by the parser.

PG-EXPR.description: Column references, positional parameters, operator invocation, row constructors and expression evaluation.
learning_objectives: Construct value expressions from column references, literals and operators.
Use positional parameters and row constructors correctly in expressions.
Explain how operator precedence and type resolution affect expression evaluation.
Predict the result type of a compound value expression.

PG-SELECT-LIST.description: Projection items, *, expressions in the select list and output column naming.
learning_objectives: Project columns and expressions in a select list.
Assign aliases that determine output column labels.
Compare SELECT * with an explicit projection and explain its stability.
Explain how PostgreSQL resolves duplicate output column names.

PG-ORDERBY.description: Sorting result rows with ORDER BY, NULLS FIRST/LAST and collation-aware ordering.
learning_objectives: Sort rows with ORDER BY on one or more sort keys.
Place nulls explicitly with NULLS FIRST or NULLS LAST.
Explain how a collation changes the ordering of text values.
Recognize that a query without ORDER BY does not guarantee row order.

PG-LIMIT.description: Bounded result retrieval with LIMIT/OFFSET and the standard FETCH syntax.
learning_objectives: Restrict a result to the first N rows with LIMIT.
Skip rows with OFFSET for simple pagination.
Use the standard FETCH FIRST syntax as an alternative to LIMIT.
Explain why LIMIT is unstable without a deterministic ORDER BY.

PG-DISTINCT.description: Duplicate removal with DISTINCT and PostgreSQL DISTINCT ON.
learning_objectives: Remove duplicate result rows with DISTINCT.
Use DISTINCT ON to keep one row per key.
Predict how NULL values are treated by duplicate removal.
Explain the sort cost that DISTINCT and DISTINCT ON can introduce.

PG-SETOPS.description: UNION, INTERSECT, EXCEPT and their ALL variants over compatible queries.
learning_objectives: Combine result sets with UNION and UNION ALL.
Use INTERSECT and EXCEPT to compare two result sets.
Ensure matching column counts and compatible types across set operations.
Explain how the ALL variants change duplicate handling.

PG-CTE.description: WITH clauses that define auxiliary statements for a larger query.
learning_objectives: Define a common table expression with a WITH clause.
Use a CTE to structure a complex query into readable stages.
Explain when PostgreSQL may materialize or inline a common table expression.
Compare a CTE with an equivalent subquery or view.

PG-RECURSIVE.description: WITH RECURSIVE iteration, termination, search order and cycle handling.
learning_objectives: Write a recursive CTE with a base case and a recursive term.
Design a termination condition that prevents infinite recursion.
Use the SEARCH and CYCLE clauses where hierarchy traversal requires them.
Explain how iteration depth affects recursive query cost.

PG-WINDOW.description: OVER, PARTITION BY, window frames and ranking/offset window functions.
learning_objectives: Apply a window function over a partition without collapsing rows.
Define a window frame for a window aggregate calculation.
Use ranking functions to number rows within partitions.
Distinguish window functions from GROUP BY aggregation.

PG-CASE.description: CASE, COALESCE, NULLIF, GREATEST and LEAST.
learning_objectives: Write searched and simple CASE expressions.
Replace NULL with COALESCE or convert it with NULLIF.
Choose between GREATEST/LEAST and CASE for value selection.
Explain the result type rules that apply to a CASE expression.

PG-NULLS.description: NULL semantics, IS NULL/IS DISTINCT FROM and how AND/OR/NOT treat unknown.
learning_objectives: Explain how SQL three-valued logic treats the unknown truth value.
Test for NULL with IS NULL and IS NOT NULL.
Use IS DISTINCT FROM for NULL-safe comparison.
Predict the result of AND, OR and NOT when an operand is unknown.

PG-AGG-FUNC.description: Set-valued aggregates, FILTER, ORDER BY inside aggregates and grouping sets.
learning_objectives: Summarize rows with aggregate functions.
Filter aggregate input rows with the FILTER clause.
Use grouping sets, ROLLUP or CUBE for multi-level summaries.
Distinguish COUNT(*) from COUNT(column) when NULL values are present.

PG-JOIN-TYPES.description: Inner, outer, cross, natural and LATERAL join semantics.
learning_objectives: Select the join variant that preserves the required rows.
Write a CROSS JOIN and explain its row count.
Use LATERAL to reference preceding FROM items.
Explain the risks of NATURAL joins in evolving schemas.

PG-TYPE-NUM.description: Integer, arbitrary-precision numeric and floating-point types, serial and arithmetic behavior.
learning_objectives: Choose between integer, numeric and floating-point types for a value.
Explain the precision and rounding behavior of numeric versus floating point.
Recognize integer overflow and integer division semantics.
Explain the storage and range differences among integer widths.

PG-TYPE-CHAR.description: character varying, character and text, padding and length semantics.
learning_objectives: Choose between varchar, char and text for a column.
Explain blank padding in fixed-length character values.
Enforce or avoid length limits with a length modifier.
Predict comparison behavior across the character types.

PG-TYPE-BOOL.description: boolean storage, accepted literals and NULL truth values.
learning_objectives: Store and query boolean values with the accepted literals.
Predict how NULL affects boolean truth values.
Use a boolean expression directly as a WHERE condition.
Compare boolean columns without redundant equality tests.

PG-TYPE-DATE.description: date, time, timestamp with/without time zone and interval.
learning_objectives: Choose between date, time and timestamp types.
Explain the difference between timestamp and timestamptz.
Perform interval arithmetic on date/time values.
Predict how the session time zone affects displayed timestamps.

PG-TYPE-JSON.description: json versus jsonb storage semantics, containment, indexing and subscripting.
learning_objectives: Compare json and jsonb storage and performance characteristics.
Query JSON values with operators and path expressions.
Test containment and key existence with jsonb operators.
Decide when JSON storage should be normalized into relational columns.

PG-TYPE-ARRAY.description: Array declaration, literals, indexing, slicing and searching.
learning_objectives: Declare and populate array columns.
Access elements and slices with array subscripts.
Search arrays with ANY, ALL and array operators.
Expand an array into rows with unnest.

PG-TYPE-MISC.description: Enumerated types, UUID, XML, network and bit-string types.
learning_objectives: Choose an enumerated type for a fixed value set.
Generate and store UUID values.
Use network and bit-string types for their intended data.
Explain the tradeoffs of enum types when the allowed values change.

PG-TYPE-RANGE.description: Built-in ranges, bounds, overlap and construction.
learning_objectives: Construct range values with explicit bounds.
Test whether ranges contain, overlap or are adjacent to one another.
Choose an index strategy for range queries.
Explain how a multirange collects disjoint range values.

PG-TYPECONV.description: Cast syntax, implicit/assignment/explicit casts and union type resolution.
learning_objectives: Cast values explicitly with CAST and the :: syntax.
Distinguish implicit, assignment and explicit cast contexts.
Predict type resolution for operators and UNION branches.
Explain when an explicit cast is required to avoid ambiguity.

PG-COLLATION.description: Collation-aware ordering and comparison, COLLATE clauses and ICU.
learning_objectives: Explain how a collation determines text ordering and comparison.
Apply COLLATE to a column or expression.
Distinguish deterministic from nondeterministic collations.
Diagnose ordering differences caused by a database or column collation.

PG-DOMAIN.description: Domains as base types with reusable CHECK constraints.
learning_objectives: Define a domain over a base type with constraints.
Reuse a domain to enforce a consistent business rule.
Explain how domain constraints interact with column constraints.
Decide when a domain is preferable to a plain constrained column.

PG-FUNC-STR.description: String operators and functions such as concatenation, substring and trim.
learning_objectives: Combine text with concatenation operators and functions.
Extract substrings and trim unwanted characters.
Replace and search text with built-in functions.
Predict NULL propagation in string expressions.

PG-FUNC-NUM.description: Numeric operators and functions such as round, trunc, mod and random.
learning_objectives: Round and truncate numeric values with the correct function.
Compute remainders and powers with numeric operators.
Generate pseudo-random values and explain their limitations.
Predict the numeric result type and rounding behavior of a function.

PG-FUNC-DATE.description: current_date/now, extract, date_trunc, age and interval arithmetic.
learning_objectives: Obtain the current date and timestamp with the built-in functions.
Extract fields from date/time values with EXTRACT.
Truncate timestamps to a chosen granularity.
Compute elapsed time with interval arithmetic.

PG-PATTERN.description: LIKE, ILIKE, SIMILAR TO and POSIX regular expressions.
learning_objectives: Match text with LIKE and ILIKE patterns.
Choose SIMILAR TO or a POSIX regular expression for complex patterns.
Escape wildcard characters in literal search terms.
Explain the performance risk of patterns that begin with a wildcard.

PG-FTS.description: tsvector/tsquery, matching @@, ranking and FTS indexing.
learning_objectives: Convert documents and queries to tsvector and tsquery.
Match documents with the @@ operator.
Rank results by relevance.
Design an index that supports full-text search.

PG-TABLE.description: CREATE TABLE, column defaults, temporary and unlogged tables.
learning_objectives: Create a table with columns, data types and defaults.
Choose temporary or unlogged tables for appropriate use cases.
Explain the lifecycle and visibility of temporary tables.
Predict the storage and durability implications of unlogged tables.

PG-IDENTITY.description: GENERATED ALWAYS/BY DEFAULT AS IDENTITY versus serial.
learning_objectives: Define an identity column with ALWAYS or BY DEFAULT.
Compare identity columns with legacy serial columns.
Explain how identity generation interacts with explicit inserts.
Identify the sequence object behind a generated key.

PG-GENCOL.description: Stored generated columns, expression rules and restrictions.
learning_objectives: Define a stored generated column with an expression.
Explain why only immutable expressions are allowed.
Compare generated columns with views and triggers.
Predict when the stored generated value is recomputed.

PG-CONSTRAINT.description: CHECK, NOT NULL and UNIQUE constraint semantics.
learning_objectives: Enforce row-level rules with CHECK and NOT NULL constraints.
Prevent duplicate values with UNIQUE constraints.
Explain how NULL values interact with UNIQUE and CHECK.
Test a constraint with both valid and invalid rows.

PG-KEYS.description: Key declaration, referential actions and deferred enforcement.
learning_objectives: Declare primary and foreign keys for related tables.
Choose a referential action for deletes and updates.
Explain deferred constraint checking inside a transaction.
Diagnose foreign-key violations caused by insertion order.

PG-ALTER.description: ALTER TABLE operations and their effects.
learning_objectives: Add, alter and drop columns with ALTER TABLE.
Predict when an ALTER TABLE operation rewrites or locks a table.
Change constraints and defaults on an existing table.
Plan a schema change that preserves existing data.

PG-SCHEMA.description: Schema organization, name resolution and the public schema.
learning_objectives: Create schemas to group related database objects.
Resolve unqualified object names through search_path.
Explain the security implications of the public schema.
Qualify objects explicitly when names could be ambiguous.

PG-VIEW.description: View semantics, updatable views and CHECK OPTION.
learning_objectives: Define a view over a query.
Query a view as if it were a table.
Explain which views are automatically updatable.
Use WITH CHECK OPTION to constrain modifications made through a view.

PG-MATVIEW.description: Materialized view storage, refresh and when to prefer them.
learning_objectives: Create and populate a materialized view.
Refresh a materialized view and explain why its data can be stale.
Compare materialized views with ordinary views.
Decide when a materialized view is worth its storage cost.

PG-PARTITION.description: Declarative range/list/hash partitioning, pruning and defaults.
learning_objectives: Choose a partitioning strategy for a large table.
Create partitions and a default partition.
Explain partition pruning during query planning.
Recognize the limitations of partitioned tables.

PG-DML.description: Data modification statements, ON CONFLICT and RETURNING.
learning_objectives: Insert, update and delete rows with the data modification statements.
Return modified rows with the RETURNING clause.
Resolve conflicts with ON CONFLICT.
Predict the rows affected by an UPDATE or DELETE predicate.

PG-MERGE.description: Conditional merge of a source table into a target.
learning_objectives: Write a MERGE statement with matched and unmatched branches.
Choose WHEN MATCHED actions for updates or deletes.
Compare MERGE with INSERT ... ON CONFLICT.
Predict MERGE behavior when the source contains duplicate keys.

PG-TXN.description: BEGIN/COMMIT/ROLLBACK, atomicity, savepoints and transaction properties.
learning_objectives: Group statements into an atomic transaction.
Roll back work with ROLLBACK or a savepoint.
Explain the atomicity and durability guarantees of a committed transaction.
Recognize operations that cannot run inside a transaction block.

PG-ISOLATION.description: Read committed, repeatable read and serializable behavior in PostgreSQL.
learning_objectives: Compare the isolation levels that PostgreSQL supports.
Explain which concurrency anomalies each isolation level prevents.
Recognize a serialization failure and retry the transaction safely.
Choose an isolation level for a concurrent workload.

PG-MVCC.description: Multiversion snapshots, visibility and their consequences.
learning_objectives: Explain how PostgreSQL keeps multiple row versions.
Describe how a snapshot determines row visibility.
Relate dead tuples to the vacuum requirement.
Predict why readers and writers generally do not block each other under MVCC.

PG-LOCK.description: Table/row locks, FOR UPDATE/SHARE, deadlocks and advisory locks.
learning_objectives: Acquire row locks with SELECT ... FOR UPDATE or FOR SHARE.
Explain how consistent lock ordering prevents deadlocks.
Read a deadlock error and choose a retry strategy.
Use advisory locks for application-level coordination.

PG-INDEX.description: Index purpose, cost, unique/partial/expression and multicolumn indexes.
learning_objectives: Explain how an index accelerates selective access.
Create partial, expression and multicolumn indexes.
Choose the column order for a multicolumn index.
Recognize the write cost of maintaining an index.

PG-INDEX-TYPES.description: B-tree, Hash, GiST, SP-GiST, GIN and BRIN selection.
learning_objectives: Match each index type to the data and operators it supports.
Explain when a GIN index is appropriate.
Use a BRIN index for a large, naturally ordered table.
Compare the storage and lookup tradeoffs of the index types.

PG-EXPLAIN.description: Reading plan trees, cost estimates, EXPLAIN ANALYZE and scan types.
learning_objectives: Read a query plan tree from the innermost node outward.
Compare estimated cost with actual execution time.
Identify sequential, index and bitmap scans in a plan.
Use EXPLAIN ANALYZE to diagnose a slow query.

PG-STATS.description: ANALYZE statistics, selectivity and statistics targets.
learning_objectives: Explain how table and column statistics guide the query planner.
Run ANALYZE and interpret its effect on a plan.
Increase the statistics target for a skewed column.
Recognize plan changes caused by stale statistics.

PG-ROLES.description: Role attributes, INHERIT, group roles and SET ROLE.
learning_objectives: Create a role with or without login capability.
Grant role membership and explain privilege inheritance.
Use SET ROLE to act with another role's privileges.
Avoid sharing a superuser role for ordinary application access.

PG-PRIVILEGE.description: GRANT/REVOKE, object privileges and grant options.
learning_objectives: Grant and revoke privileges on database objects.
Explain which privileges a role needs to complete a task.
Use WITH GRANT OPTION and explain its risk.
Audit the effective privileges of a role.

PG-RLS.description: Policies, USING/WITH CHECK, permissive vs restrictive and bypass rules.
learning_objectives: Enable row-level security on a table.
Write USING and WITH CHECK policies for access control.
Explain how permissive and restrictive policies combine.
Identify the roles that bypass row-level security.

PG-UDF.description: CREATE FUNCTION, arguments, volatility categories and SETOF results.
learning_objectives: Define a function with typed arguments and a return type.
Choose the correct volatility category for a function.
Return a set of rows with SETOF.
Explain how volatility affects planner behavior.

PG-PLPGSQL.description: Blocks, declarations, control structures, statements and exceptions.
learning_objectives: Structure a PL/pgSQL program with declaration and body blocks.
Use IF/ELSIF and loop constructs for control flow.
Declare and assign variables inside a PL/pgSQL function.
Handle errors with EXCEPTION blocks.

PG-PROC.description: CREATE PROCEDURE, CALL and transaction control in procedures.
learning_objectives: Create and invoke a procedure with CREATE PROCEDURE and CALL.
Use transaction control statements inside a procedure.
Distinguish procedures from functions.
Choose a procedure when a task needs multiple transactions.

PG-TRIGGER.description: Trigger timing, row/statement granularity, NEW/OLD and trigger functions.
learning_objectives: Create a trigger that fires before or after a data change.
Choose row-level or statement-level trigger timing.
Access NEW and OLD row values inside a trigger function.
Explain the performance and recursion risks of triggers.

PG-CONFIG.description: postgresql.conf, ALTER SYSTEM and key resource settings.
learning_objectives: Locate and interpret key PostgreSQL configuration parameters.
Change a setting with ALTER SYSTEM and apply it with reload or restart.
Distinguish session, database and cluster-level settings.
Tune a resource parameter and observe its effect.

PG-VACUUM.description: VACUUM variants, autovacuum, visibility map and wraparound.
learning_objectives: Explain why dead tuples accumulate and require vacuuming.
Run VACUUM and VACUUM ANALYZE appropriately.
Describe autovacuum's role and triggering conditions.
Recognize transaction ID wraparound risk.

PG-BACKUP.description: SQL dump, file-system backup, PITR and their tradeoffs.
learning_objectives: Choose between logical dumps and physical backups.
Perform a logical backup with pg_dump and restore it.
Explain how point-in-time recovery uses a base backup and archived WAL.
Verify a backup before relying on it.

PG-WAL.description: WAL purpose, durability and archiving basics.
learning_objectives: Explain why changes are written to WAL before data files.
Describe how checkpoints bound recovery time.
Configure WAL archiving for point-in-time recovery.
Relate WAL settings to durability and write throughput.

PG-REPLICATION.description: Physical vs logical replication, streaming and slots.
learning_objectives: Compare physical and logical replication.
Describe how a standby streams and applies WAL.
Explain the role of replication slots.
Choose a replication approach for a failover or data-distribution requirement.

PG-MONITOR.description: Cumulative statistics views and activity monitoring.
learning_objectives: Inspect active sessions with pg_stat_activity.
Identify expensive statements using statistics views.
Interpret cumulative statistics for tables and indexes.
Design a monitoring check for a database health condition.
